definition_quote.value: The practice of professional nursing as a registered nurse means the performance of professional nursing services by a person who holds a valid license pursuant to the terms of this chapter, and who bears primary responsibility and accountability for nursing practices based on specialized knowledge, judgment, and skill derived from the principles of biological, physical, and behavioral sciences.
definition_quote.quote: "The practice of professional nursing" as a registered nurse means the performance of professional nursing services by a person who holds a valid license pursuant to the terms of this chapter, and who bears primary responsibility and accountability for nursing practices based on specialized knowledge, judgment, and skill derived from the principles of biological, physical, and behavioral sciences.

value: Assessing human responses to actual or potential health conditions
Advocating provision of health-care services through collaboration
Executing regimens prescribed by licensed physician, dentist, podiatrist, or APRN
Administering, supervising, delegating, and evaluating nursing activities
Making a pronouncement of death (in specified settings)
methods_authorized.quote: Assessing human responses to actual or potential health conditions; Identifying the needs of the individual or family by developing a nursing diagnosis; Implementing nursing interventions based on the nursing diagnosis; Teaching health-care practices; Advocating the provision of health-care services through collaboration with other health service personnel; Executing regimens, as prescribed by a licensed physician, dentist, podiatrist, or advanced practice registered nurse, including the dispensing or administration of medications and treatments; Administering, supervising, delegating, and evaluating nursing activities

impaired_nurse_alternative_program_avail.quote: "Alternative program" means a nondisciplinary monitoring program approved by a licensing board.

rn_death_pronouncement_authorized.quote: A registered nurse shall have the authority, as part of the practice of professional nursing, to make a pronouncement of death; provided, however, that this provision shall only apply to attending nurses caring for terminally ill patients or patients who have "do not resuscitate" orders in the home or place of residence of the deceased as a part of a hospice program or a certified home health-care agency program; in a skilled nursing facility; in a residential community associated with a skilled nursing facility; any licensed assisted living community; in an extended care facility; or in a hospice
